Natalie — thanks. Quick thoughts on structure and resilience for a virtual full-loop:

Proposed running order (to minimize cognitive switching and warmup cost):
1) System design (60 min) — heavier cognitive load, do first while candidate fresh.
2) Short 20–30 minute respite (candidate rest + panel reset).
3) Coding deep-dive (50 min) — focused pair-coding/exercises.
4) 10-minute micro-break.
5) Product / behavioral (40 min) — cross-functional discussion.
6) 15-minute break.
7) On-call / reliability + culture (30 min) — lighter closeout session.

Notes / operational items:
- Scribe: Jasmine can be scribe and owner of the shared debrief doc (jasmine_liu@redwood.com). Jasmine — can you keep the debrief doc open during each interview and capture 3 ratings + 2 bullet reasons?
- Panelist order: rotate senior ICs so the same person doesn't interview twice in a row. Kimberly — are you able to take System design? Marissa — can you hold Coding?
- Respite windows: candidate asked for a longer break after slot 1 — we should confirm 25 minutes. That still fits the 4-hour block with short breaks later.
- Zoom rooms: we'll use separate meeting links per session with a single calendar invite containing all links. I'll add the drive agenda and rubric link in the invite.

I attached a lightly updated agenda (see Drive link). If this order looks good I'll coordinate exact panelist times and send final calendar invites to Samira.

Best,
